message:
fix(engine lifecycle): wire the terminate+restart fallback (#233) (#291)

The transport kill mechanism existed end-to-end (SidecarPort.kill ->
engine_kill -> Child::kill) but the product flow never reached it:

- SidecarClient.shutdown() timed out on a wedged worker and just marked
  the client closed — the zombie process kept the Rust ENGINE slot, so
  the next spawn raced it into ENGINE_ALREADY_RUNNING. shutdown() now
  falls back to port.kill() after the graceful window, plus a short
  exit wait so a respawn cannot outrun the dying process.
- New SidecarClient.terminate(): immediate kill for the cancel-escalation
  path (a worker mid-inference cannot answer a graceful request anyway).
- TranscriptionSession.cancelTranscription() waits cancelGraceMs
  (default 4s, injectable) for the terminal event after the job.cancel
  ack; on expiry it marks the job 'cancelled' BEFORE the kill so the
  exit path cannot label it a crash, terminates the worker, and
  respawns a fresh engine. Audio / prior score / project state live
  outside the worker and are untouched.
- restartEngine() now awaits the old shutdown instead of fire-and-forget,
  and job/state callbacks are guarded to the current client so a
  replaced worker's late frames cannot downgrade the fresh engine.
- MockSidecarPort gains simulateBlockingInference() (dispatch alive,
  job thread non-interruptible) and closeStdin() is a no-op while
  wedged — matching the real worker's debug.hang semantics.

Tests: cancel escalation ends 'cancelled' with a fresh ready engine,
cooperative cancel never kills, restartEngine kills a wedged worker,
shutdown() kill fallback, terminate() rejects pending requests.
521 vitest + tsc + eslint clean.
